resources.string: Shows and controls the current media playback in a single row.
Notification access not granted. Tap to set it up.
Nothing is playing. Tap to open your player.
Access not granted. The widget cannot see any player yet.
Android only lets apps with notification access read active media sessions. Notifications themselves are never read or stored.

Android may block this access for apps installed from outside an app store. In that case, open the app info of Media Widget, tap the three-dot menu in the top right corner, choose \"Allow restricted settings\" and try again.
You can revoke the access at any time using the button below.
No active media session. The widget shows the last played track:
No players detected yet. Start playback in a player and it shows up here.
All players detected so far. The widget ignores players that are turned off.
Tap the star to choose your favorite. The widget always prefers it over other players, and a tap on "Nothing is playing" opens it.

Android sends play to the player that was active last. If that is a turned-off player, the widget shows the open symbol on the cover and the play button instead. Tapping it opens the shown player and starts playback.
Swipe a player to the left to forget it. It shows up again as soon as it is used again. Uninstalled players are removed automatically.
If several players are active, the widget shows a switch button next to the title.
All players are turned off. Turn on at least one player, otherwise the widget cannot show or control anything.
Extra CPU load: about %1$d %% of one core while music is playing and the screen is on.

While music is playing, a subtle fill grows behind the widget from left to right and shows how far the song has played. The widget is only refreshed while your screen is on and unlocked. Each refresh takes about 0.15 s of CPU time (measured on a test device), so shorter intervals move more smoothly but use more battery. 5 s is a good balance.

If the widget sometimes stops updating, Android may be restricting the app in the background. Open the app info, go to \"App battery usage\" and choose \"Unrestricted\". The exact names can differ depending on your device.
Long-press an empty spot on your home screen, choose \"Widgets\", find \"Media Widget\" and drag \"Media controls\" onto the home screen.
A rather long song title that needs to be ellipsized
